-- IGProtocol scaffold: VINIT → FSPLIT → EVALT → EVALF → AFWD → TANCH → IFIX
-- (native ob3ect designer; elaborate against the kernel to verify)
name: the least order of a bipartite graph whose list

phase_0.boundary_condition: the class of all finite bipartite graphs, each equipped with an order and a list chromatic number
phase_0.domain_name: the least order of a bipartite graph whose list
phase_0.justification: Auto-designed by the native Ob3ect Auto-Designer (in-process candle, no Python)

AFWD.chosen_element: the function extracting the order (number of vertices) from a bipartite graph
AFWD.justification: the affirmative graphs are mapped to their orders, moving from concrete witnesses to the numerical quantity the object names

AREV.chosen_element: the inverse mapping that would translate an order back to a candidate graph (not used, but available)
AREV.justification: a reversal of AFWD could reconstruct a witness graph from the order, but the search proceeds forward only

CLINK.chosen_element: composition of successive probes across candidate orders (unfolded form, not used in the compact structural reading)
CLINK.justification: if the search were expanded stepwise, CLINK would chain the failure of one order to the check of the next, but the object encodes the limit directly

ENGAGR.chosen_element: a hypothetical state where a graph simultaneously has and lacks a list coloring exceeding b, which would be a paraconsistent B resolution
ENGAGR.justification: in the well‑defined finite setting no such overlap occurs, but the token marks that the structure is paraconsistent and can contain such a truth if the underlying definitions were ever to contradict

EVALF.chosen_element: the set of bipartite graphs whose list chromatic number does not exceed b
EVALF.justification: this arm is the complement and is discarded; it contains no graphs that can contribute to the least order

EVALT.chosen_element: the set of bipartite graphs whose list chromatic number exceeds b
EVALT.justification: this arm collects the witnesses that satisfy the property; among them the minimal order will be selected

FFUSE.chosen_element: no reunion of the two arms is performed
FFUSE.justification: the fork stays open because the negative arm (graphs with chi_l ≤ b) is irrelevant to naming the least order; only the positive arm reaches the terminal anchor

FSPLIT.chosen_element: the condition chi_l(G) > b, applied to every finite bipartite graph G
FSPLIT.justification: the entire domain of candidate graphs bifurcates precisely into those that exceed the bound and those that do not; this split creates the two arms that drive the search

IFIX.chosen_element: the least order, once found, is fixed as a permanent record
IFIX.justification: the result is appended immutably to the output so that the search terminates with a definite value

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: the self-reference of the bound b, which remains unchanged throughout
IMSCRIB.justification: the bound is not transformed; it simply persists as the reference against which graphs are evaluated

TANCH.chosen_element: the smallest order among those projected from the affirmative arm
TANCH.justification: once the minimal order is identified, the search closes under this terminal anchor; it is the answer the structure was designed to isolate

VINIT.chosen_element: the bound b is accepted as a given parameter, and the search space is not yet populated
VINIT.justification: the problem begins with no candidate graph instantiated and no order considered; only the required threshold exists

phase_2.fuse_element: none — the fork is permanently open
phase_2.fuse_result: the arms are never reunited; the negative arm is irrelevant to the computation of the least order
phase_2.rejoin_note: the fork stays open and does not rejoin. The positive arm passes through order extraction and into the terminal anchor; the negative arm is discarded. The kernel judges the structural closure over SIXTEEN_3 without a FFUSE.
phase_2.split_element: the predicate chi_l(G) > b on finite bipartite graphs
phase_2.split_input: a finite bipartite graph G together with the bound b
phase_2.verdict_reason: FSPLIT3 at step 2 dangles — no matching FFUSE3

phase_3.both_description: B4 B (11) — a contradictory overlapping of T and F, not realized under standard list coloring but structurally available
phase_3.false_description: B4 F (10) — the negative condition where a graph's list chromatic number ≤ b
phase_3.true_description: B4 T (01) — the affirmative condition where a bipartite graph has list chromatic number > b
phase_3.void_description: B4 N (00) — the initial void before any graph is considered; nothing is established

steps.domain_action: the bound b is accepted, and the space of bipartite graphs is void
every finite bipartite graph splits into two arms based on chi_l(G) > b
the arm of graphs with list chromatic number exceeding b is affirmed
the arm of graphs with list chromatic number ≤ b is discarded
each graph on the affirmative arm is mapped to its order
the smallest order among the projected values is fixed as the result
the least order is recorded permanently

phase_5.alfs_store: the axiomatic foundations of finite combinatorics and list coloring provide the bootstrap store for this object
phase_5.compiler_frontend: the definitions of bipartite graph, list assignment, and proper coloring form the domain‑specific semantics that determine the predicate chi_l > b
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: comparison across the space of graphs is implicit; the structure does not require explicit message passing because all graphs are available in the domain
phase_5.memory_mechanism: the object stores the bound b persistently; intermediate states (candidate graphs) exist only as arms of the fork
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: the search for the minimum is structural rather than iterative; the terminal anchor directly picks the least order from the affirmative arm

phase_6.cycle_cost: the conceptual effort of evaluating the list chromatic number for every candidate graph, which is abstracted away by the structural fork
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the structural mapping neither creates nor destroys information; it reorganizes the same domain into the extremal value without loss
phase_6.post_cycle_state: the minimal order is identified and fixed, and the negative arm is discarded
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: the least order is unknown; all bipartite graphs are undifferentiated
